_comment: The controlled vocabulary for scripts/suggest-tags.js. This file is the ONLY
source of allowed tags: it is compiled into a JSON Schema enum, so the model
cannot invent a tag even if it wants to — an off-list value is rejected by the
API before it ever reaches us.
Every one of the 27 tags already present in the Airtable base appears below,
spelled exactly as it is stored there. Airtable's Tags field is a select field:
sending an option that does not already exist returns
INVALID_MULTIPLE_CHOICE_OPTIONS and rejects the whole batch. So any tag marked
"new": true must be added as an option in Airtable before apply-tags.js can
write it — scripts/apply-tags.js checks this for you and names the missing ones.
Descriptions are written for the model, not for humans browsing the site. Say
what the tag covers AND what it excludes; ambiguous descriptions are the main

facets.name: Topic
facets.guidance: What the item is substantively about. Include every topic a researcher filtering the library would genuinely expect this item to appear under, and nothing beyond that. The limit is a ceiling, not a target: most items warrant two or three, and a broad survey or framework paper may warrant five.

tags.name: Evaluations
tags.description: Benchmarks, capability tests, or evaluation methodology for measuring what AI models can do in biology. Use for the benchmark or eval itself, and for critiques of eval practice. Not for risk assessment frameworks — use 'Risk assessments'.

tags.name: Risk assessments
tags.description: Structured methods for assessing risk from a model or tool, including uplift studies and risk-scoring tools. Distinguished from 'Evaluations': evaluations measure capability, risk assessments reason about consequence and likelihood.

tags.name: Threat Assessment
tags.description: Characterising the threat landscape — who the actors are, what pathways exist, how the deliberate-misuse picture is changing. Descriptive and strategic rather than measurement-focused.

tags.name: Capabilities
tags.description: Analysis of what frontier models are actually capable of in a biological context, including capability thresholds and forecasts. Use alongside 'Evaluations' only when capability trends are a distinct subject, not the measurement method.

tags.name: Mitigations
tags.description: Technical or procedural safeguards that reduce misuse risk — refusal training, unlearning, access controls, safeguard evaluation, tamper resistance. Not policy instruments; use 'Policy' for those.

tags.name: Pretraining
tags.description: Interventions at the pretraining stage specifically: training-data filtering, corpus curation, deep-ignorance approaches. A narrower sibling of 'Mitigations'.

tags.name: Prevention
tags.description: Upstream measures that stop a biological threat from being created or acquired at all, as opposed to detecting or responding to one.

tags.name: Biological Tools
tags.description: Biological design tools and AI-for-biology models as a category — BDTs, bio-foundation models, genome and protein language models — including their governance and risk management. Use 'Protein design' for protein-structure-specific work.

tags.name: Protein design
tags.description: AI-driven protein structure prediction and de novo protein design, and the biosecurity implications thereof.

tags.name: LLMs
tags.description: General-purpose large language models as the subject — chatbot uplift, model releases, LLM safeguards. Not for bio-specific sequence models; use 'Biological Tools'.

tags.name: Open-weight LLMs
tags.description: Risks, governance, and safeguard durability specific to models whose weights are publicly released.

tags.name: AI agents
tags.description: Autonomous or semi-autonomous AI systems that plan and act — AI co-scientists, agentic benchmarks, lab automation agents, end-to-end research agents. NEW.

tags.name: Nucleic acid synthesis screening
tags.description: Screening of DNA/RNA synthesis orders, sequences of concern, gene synthesis oversight, and mail-order DNA biosecurity. NEW.

tags.name: Cloud labs
tags.description: Remotely operated and automated laboratories, and the access pathway they create between a digital design and physical material.

tags.name: Virology
tags.description: Virology-specific capability, knowledge, or risk — including virology benchmarks and viral escape prediction.

tags.name: Synthetic biology
tags.description: Synthetic biology and genome engineering as a field, including how AI is changing its practice. NEW.

tags.name: Pandemic preparedness
tags.description: Preparedness, early warning, detection, and response to biological events — including AI-enabled biosurveillance and resilience. NEW.

tags.name: Attribution and forensics
tags.description: Tracing an engineered biological agent to its source; bioforensics; deterrence that depends on attribution. NEW.

tags.name: Jailbreaks and red-teaming
tags.description: Adversarial testing of safeguards — jailbreak attacks, red-team exercises, violet teaming, safeguard circumvention. NEW.

tags.name: Data governance
tags.description: Governance of biological data itself — access to sequence and experimental datasets, training-data provenance, data-sharing regimes. NEW.

tags.name: Metadata
tags.description: Metadata standards and exchange formats for biodesign, provenance, and traceability.

tags.name: Taxonomy
tags.description: Classification schemes and typologies — of mitigations, risks, capabilities, or actors.

tags.name: Framework
tags.description: A named framework, standard, or structured methodology proposed for adoption. Use when the framework is the contribution, not merely referenced.

tags.name: Transparency and reporting
tags.description: Disclosure practices — model cards, system cards, safety-framework publication, standards for reporting evaluation results. NEW.

tags.name: Policy
tags.description: Policy analysis and recommendations directed at governments or regulators. Use for the policy substance; 'Comment / Statement' and 'Request for Information (RFI)' describe the document's form instead.

tags.name: International governance
tags.description: Multilateral and cross-border governance — treaty regimes, the BWC, UN processes, international summits, red lines, cross-national coordination. NEW.

tags.name: Dual-use research
tags.description: The dual-use dilemma itself — benefit/risk balancing, dual-use review processes, responsible-innovation norms. NEW.

tags.name: Health security
tags.description: Benefits and opportunities of AI in biology for health and biosecurity, rather than the misuse risk. Use for items whose main argument is upside. NEW.

tags.name: Cyberbiosecurity
tags.description: The security of biological infrastructure, instrumentation, and data pipelines as cyber-physical systems. NEW.

tags.name: Bioweapons history
tags.description: Historical bioweapons programmes and past acquisition attempts, and the lessons drawn from them for the AI era. NEW.

tags.name: Non-state actors
tags.description: Terrorist groups, lone actors, and other non-state threats — barriers to acquisition, novice uplift framed around who is being uplifted. NEW.

facets.name: Document kind
facets.guidance: Only where the document's form is not already captured by the Item Type field (which separately records Report, Preprint, Journal article, Blog post, Webpage, Book, and so on). Leave empty for an ordinary article, report, or paper — most records should get nothing here.

tags.name: Request for Information (RFI)
tags.description: A submitted response to a government request for information or public consultation. In this library these are overwhelmingly responses to the NIST RFI on chemical and biological AI models — pair with the 'NIST' tag when so.

tags.name: Comment / Statement
tags.description: A public statement, open letter, joint statement, or op-ed-style position piece signed by an organisation or group of experts.

tags.name: Event report
tags.description: Proceedings, summaries, or readouts from a workshop, conference, roundtable, or summit.

facets.name: Jurisdiction
facets.guidance: Only when the item is specifically about that jurisdiction's policy, institutions, or strategic position. Do NOT tag by the author's nationality or the publisher's location — a US think tank writing about global risk is not 'United States'.

tags.name: United States
tags.description: US federal policy, legislation, agencies, or national security posture.

tags.name: United Kingdom
tags.description: UK policy, institutions such as AISI, or national strategy.

tags.name: European Union
tags.description: EU policy and law, including the EU AI Act. NEW.

tags.name: Australia
tags.description: Australian policy and national strategy.

tags.name: China
tags.description: Chinese policy, capability, or US–China dynamics. NEW.

tags.name: Global South
tags.description: Governance, capacity, and equity concerns for lower- and middle-income countries. NEW.

facets.name: Named body or initiative
facets.guidance: Only when the item is directed at, responding to, or substantially about that specific body or initiative. Do NOT use this to record the author's own organisation — the Institution field already does that, and duplicating it here makes the tag facet useless.

tags.name: NIST
tags.description: The item responds to or analyses NIST activity — most often the NIST RFI on safety considerations for chemical and biological AI models.

tags.name: Department of Homeland Security
tags.description: DHS reporting, mandates, or programmes are the subject.

tags.name: AI Action Plan
tags.description: The US AI Action Plan specifically.

tags.name: Anthropic
tags.description: Anthropic's own safeguards, model policy, or research are the subject of the item.
